alerts.title: Abdominal pain on TLD: screen for ADR and non-drug causes
alerts.message: Guidelines require all health workers to screen every encounter for suspected adverse drug reactions and record any symptom, including mild ones, in the ART card and HMIS. The patient reports new abdominal pain without fever on TDF/3TC/DTG and a good appetite, and the clinician's plan records no evaluation, examination findings beyond appetite and fever, or ADR screening. The excerpts list abdominal complaints such as right upper quadrant pain with hepatotoxicity and pancreatitis as drug-related symptoms to review, but they do not establish that TLD causes this patient's pain. Abdominal pain may also have non-drug causes that need assessment. Attribution is therefore undetermined.

evidence.recommended_action: Complete and document the Drug Safety Screening checklist, characterise the pain (location, duration, jaundice, nausea, vomiting), examine the abdomen, and report any suspected ADR through HMIS and the ADR form.
